question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{75}$ be a random sample of size $n=75$ from a population with probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{{x}^{4}}, & x\ge 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=0.75,$ calculate $P(1.5<\overset{―}{X}<1.6).$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8159\,$ | $\,0.8186\,$ | $\,0.8212\,$ |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8413\,$ | $\,0.8438\,$ | $\,0.8461\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8643\,$ | $\,0.8665\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =75,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{3}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{b\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{b}\frac{3}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{b\to \infty }{[-\frac{3}{2{x}^{2}}]}_{1}^{b} \\  & ={lim}_{b\to \infty }[\frac{3}{2}-\frac{3}{2{b}^{2}}] \\  & =\frac{3}{2} \\  & =1.5,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is ${\sigma }^{2}=0.75.$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(1.5,\frac{0.75}{75}) \\  & ∼N(1.5,0.01).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(1.5<\overset{―}{X}<1.6).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1.5<\overset{―}{X}<1.6) & =P(\frac{1.5-1.5}{\sqrt{0.01}}<Z<\frac{1.6-1.5}{\sqrt{0.01}}) \\  & =P(0<Z<1) \\  & =P(Z<1)-P(Z<0) \\  & =Φ(1)-Φ(0)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
Φ(1)=0.8413,
$$

and by the symmetry of the normal distribution, $Φ(0)=0.5.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1.5<\overset{―}{X}<1.6) & =Φ(1)-Φ(0) \\  & =0.8413-0.5 \\  & =0.3413.\end{aligned}
$$
